It centralises the repetitive JSON unmarshal used by existence\n// checks across the codebase.\nfunc queryExists(sql string) (bool, error) {\n\tout, err := dbQuery(sql)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tvar rows []struct {\n\t\tOne int `json:\"1\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(out, &rows); err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\treturn len(rows) > 0, nil\n}\n\n// queryRows runs a query and unmarshals the JSON result set into dest, which\n// must be a pointer to a slice. It is\n// used by idempotent migration functions to decide whether to run ALTER TABLE.\nfunc tableHasColumn(table, column string) (bool, error) {\n\tout, err := dbQuery(fmt.Sprintf(\"PRAGMA table_info(%s);\", table))\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tvar cols []struct {\n\t\tName string `json:\"name\"`\n\t}\n\tif err := json.Unmarshal(out, &cols); err != nil {\n\t\treturn false, err\n\t}\n\tfor _, c := range cols {\n\t\tif c.Name == column {\n\t\t\treturn true, nil\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn false, nil\n}\n\n// dbExec runs a SQL statement through the sqlite3 CLI. An empty result is normalized to the JSON array \"[]\" so that\n// callers always receive a consistent array representation.\nfunc dbQuery(sql string) ([]byte, error) {\n\tcmd := exec.Command(\"sqlite3\", \"-json\", dbPath, sql)\n\tvar stderr bytes.Buffer\n\tcmd.Stderr = &stderr\n\tout, err := cmd.Output()\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"sqlite3 query: %v: %s\", err, stderr.String())\n\t}\n\tif len(out) == 0 {\n\t\treturn []byte(\"[]\"), nil\n\t}\n\treturn out, nil\n}\n\n// initDB creates the schema and marks the current schema version.
